_comment: Theme definitions written for Bezalel. prune.py puts them in data/reformed_evangelical/themes.json, replacing a definition with the same key. Each is a key kept Owen entries use (or a parent of one) whose upstream definition is missing (it lived in the excluded heiser, bradley or synthesis folders) or describes an excluded author's argument. Key works name only material that ships.

themes.description: How Scripture describes what Christ's death accomplishes: sacrifice, ransom and redemption, propitiation, reconciliation, substitution and representation, and victory over the powers.
Christ bore in the sinner's place the penalty due to sin, satisfying God's holy justice. Affirmed by Owen as a true juridical facet of the cross.

themes.theme_label: The Work of the Holy Spirit
themes.description: The person and work of the Holy Spirit — regeneration, indwelling, filling, comfort, assurance, and the fruit he produces.

Humanity created in the image and likeness of God (Genesis 1:26-27; 9:6), and Christ as the image of the invisible God into whose likeness believers are being transformed (Colossians 1:15; 2 Corinthians 3:18; Romans 8:29).
Adam and Christ as representative heads whose acts carry consequences for those joined to them: in Adam all die, in Christ all are made alive (Romans 5:12-21; 1 Corinthians 15:21-22, 45-49).
